lead_headline: Six new restaurant leads land—Dry Dock Pub Wash Park, Spicy Kitchen Westminster, Port of Subs Littleton, plus two more reopenings—while liquor license freeze enters day 24 with zero state response

restaurant.blurb: Six opening leads today: Dry Dock Pub taking over Wash Park brewpub space, Spicy Kitchen food-truck-to-brick in Westminster, Port of Subs expanding Littleton, plus The Little Kitchen Barnum, Tacos el Comando Aurora, Denver Café & Kava Park Hill. Three closures: Lucile's Creole 15-year run ends, nook Coffee shuttered.

liquor.blurb: Day 24 of total system collapse — Colorado's liquor license database remains in complete suspended animation with zero applications filed, zero status updates, zero administrative activity since the April 30 cutoff. The blackout now consumes nearly a full month as the entire May application cycle vanishes without trace. All 12,396 tracked licenses frozen in administrative purgatory with no state acknowledgment of the outage, no contingency plan announced, no timeline for restoration, no explanation offered to applicants whose businesses hang in limbo. The regulatory void deepens as the invisible backlog compounds behind bureaucratic walls while officials maintain absolute radio silence on when—or if—normal operations resume.

reputation.blurb: One mention yesterday, a 1970s Denver infrastructure throwback on Instagram — weekly tally climbs to 64 across 11 sources, up sharply from last week's 48 (+33% gain). Instagram dominates with 26 mentions (41% of total), Reddit adds 11, Denver Post 7, Facebook 6, X/Twitter 4. Google News RSS remains primary discovery channel at 97% (62 of 64). The week shows accelerated pickup velocity compared to prior period's slower accumulation, pushing toward monthly close of 220 mentions — well above typical baseline as May tracking enters final stretch with momentum intact.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) breaks the six-day zero streak — a single addition ends the longest acquisition freeze of May but barely registers against the broader stall. MTD advances to +23 (+1.0/day), 90-day net holds at +135. The past seven days show +2 total (16 new, 14 canceled), collapsing from the prior week's +7 as churn accelerates and new subscriber velocity flatlines. May's pattern crystallizes: a concentrated May 12-15 surge delivered the bulk of monthly gains, then immediate silence through a week-long drought, now a lone subscriber trickles through. YTD pace of +1.3/day continues outpacing the MTD crawl, but the divergence underscores how thoroughly momentum evaporated after mid-month as daily activity compresses to near-dormancy following what was briefly sustained growth.
